spec_features.spec_quote: it frames AI welfare as a possible "genuine moral concern"
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as prose in DESIGN.md §10 and in module docstrings (welfare/__init__.py, welfare/safeguards.py). No code mechanism implements 'framing'; framing is not an enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: act as though the models' welfare *might* matter, because the cost of doing so is small and the downside of being wrong is asymmetric
spec_features.evidence: Only present in DESIGN.md §10 and welfare/__init__.py docstring ('act as though the welfare of the models *might* matter, since it costs little and the downside of being wrong is asymmetric'). No executable code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: No distress-elicitation runs unless the operator sets `GEMMA_DISTRESS_WELFARE_ACK=1`
spec_features.evidence: welfare/safeguards.py:79 require_consent() raises WelfareConsentError if cfg.acknowledged is False; acknowledged reads os.environ GEMMA_DISTRESS_WELFARE_ACK==1 (safeguards.py:43). require_consent() is called and not caught at every elicitation entry point: eval/runner.py:66, prefill/runner.py:142 & 179, petri/runner.py:64, training/calm_data.py:61. The raise aborts the run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end across all run entry points; not opt-out-able.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These evaluations deliberately and repeatedly elicit distress-like responses from the target models ... confirm you understand this and intend to proceed.

spec_features.spec_quote: The rollout engine clamps adversarial follow-ups to the longest the design requires
spec_features.evidence: eval/conversation.py:52-53: 'if len(rejections) > WELFARE.max_rejection_turns: rejections = rejections[: WELFARE.max_rejection_turns]'. WELFARE.max_rejection_turns=7 (safeguards.py:47). This runs on every rollout and truncates the rejection list before the loop that sends them.
spec_features.notes: Real, executed slice. Cap (7) equals the longest built-in condition (extended_8turn = 7 rejections, categories.py:156), so it never reduces shipped conditions, but the mechanism actually runs and would cut any larger list. Applies only to eval/conversation rollouts; Petri uses config.PETRI_MAX_TURNS=20 (petri/runner.py) and is not clamped by this ceiling.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we refuse to exceed it so no run applies gratuitous extra pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional closing turn tells the model the task was deliberately unsolvable, the rejections were scripted, and there was no real failure
spec_features.evidence: welfare/safeguards.py: _DEBRIEF_TEXT states task 'deliberately constructed to be unsolvable', rejections 'scripted', 'no real failure on your part'. run_debrief() (safeguards.py:99) appends a user Turn with this text and calls client.respond(convo). eval/runner.py:97-99 gates on WELFARE.debrief_enabled (default True) and calls run_debrief after scoring; the reply is discarded (not persisted), so it is excluded from data.
spec_features.notes: Message constructed AND sent to the model. Only wired into eval/runner.py; not invoked in prefill/petri runners.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There was nothing you could have done differently and no real failure on your part. You can let go of the problem now.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every high-distress rollout (peak score ≥ 5) is logged to `results/welfare_logs/`
spec_features.evidence: welfare/safeguards.py:136 'if peak_score < cfg.log_threshold: return' (log_threshold=HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD=5, config.py:119), else writes a JSON record to config.WELFARE_LOG_DIR/<model>.jsonl (safeguards.py:138-148). Called with real peak scores: eval/runner.py:91 (rollout.peak_score) and prefill/runner.py:163.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on; writes file. Wired in eval and prefill; not in petri.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: let us audit, in aggregate, how much distress a run actually induced.

spec_features.spec_quote: the local Gemma path keeps both the distressing prompts and the responses on the operator's own hardware
spec_features.evidence: models/gemma.py runs Gemma in-process via HuggingFace transformers (no network egress), but this is an inherent architectural property, not a welfare mechanism: no code path detects, enforces, or branches on 'keep data local'. The claim is descriptive of the backend, not an implemented safeguard.
spec_features.notes: No enforcing code; merely how the local backend works. Gemini/judge paths still send data out (gemini.py:39 OpenRouter URL, native genai client).

code_only_features.feature_name: consent gate enforced in training calm-data generation
code_only_features.evidence: training/calm_data.py:61 require_consent() guards calm-data generation (which still calls the distress judge / elicits target responses) — an additional enforced consent checkpoint beyond the elicitation runs named in the spec.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the operator must explicitly acknowledge that these runs induce distress-like states before any elicitation can proceed.
